title: The Leader Who Does Not Pray
subtitle: Prayer is the first thing to go in a busy ministry and the last thing anyone notices is gone, which is exactly why it is the truest measure of a leader's soul.

sections.title: The First Thing to Go
sections.body:
When a leader gets busy, prayer goes first. Not because he decides it matters least, but because it is the one thing nobody schedules for him and nobody checks.

The sermon has a deadline. The meeting has a time. The hospital visit has a bed and a name and a family waiting. All of these push back when you neglect them. Prayer does not push back. You can skip it for a week and the church runs. You can skip it for a month and the lights stay on. You can skip it for a year and still be widely regarded as a man of God, because the work continues and the work is what people see.

So prayer becomes the soft place in the schedule, the thing that yields to everything harder, and a man can lose it slowly without ever choosing to. He does not quit praying. He just keeps being too busy to start.

The first thing to go. The last thing anyone misses. That is the danger in a sentence.

sections.title: Talking About God Instead of to Him
sections.body:
Here is the cruelest part. A pastor's job lets him fake a prayer life without quite knowing he is faking it.

He reads Scripture, but for the sermon. He thinks about God all day, but as the subject of his work. He says words over meals and meetings and the sick, and the words are real prayers, but they are public and brief and aimed at an audience. And all of this religious activity fills the space where private communion used to be, until a man can go weeks speaking constantly about God and almost never speaking to Him.

The study is not the prayer closet. Preparing to talk to people about God is not the same act as talking to God yourself, and a lifetime of confusing the two is how a famous preacher ends up a stranger to the One he preaches. The proximity is the trap. No one is closer to the things of God all day, and no one is more able to substitute the work for the relationship and call it the same thing.

You can handle holy things daily and grow cold to the Holy One. Ask any of us. We know.

sections.title: What Your Prayerlessness Is Actually Saying
sections.body:
Prayerlessness is never only a time problem. It is a belief problem wearing a schedule for a disguise.

When a leader does not pray, he is announcing, with his calendar, that he believes the work depends on him. He has, somewhere in his functional theology, concluded that his planning matters more than God's power, that the outcome rides on his competence, and that the hour spent on his knees would be better spent on his feet. He would never say this. He says it every morning with his alarm clock.

The leader who prays little is telling the truth about who he thinks runs the church. Not the God he names from the pulpit. Himself. Prayerlessness is practical atheism in a man who would die for the doctrine, and that gap between the doctrine and the knees is the most honest thing about him.

Show me your prayer life and I will show you what you actually believe about God. Not what you preach about Him. What you believe.

sections.title: How Men Who Lasted Actually Prayed
sections.body:
The leaders who endured did not pray more impressively. They prayed more stubbornly.

Jesus, with more demands on Him than any of us will ever carry, rose before light and went to a solitary place to pray, and when the crowds came looking He had already been with the Father and could face them from fullness instead of fumes. He did not pray because His schedule was clear. He prayed because His schedule was crushing, and He knew which direction the help came from.

The pattern in the men who finished well is not complicated. A fixed time, guarded like an appointment with the only Person who can be trusted with the whole weight. A real conversation, not a performance, with confession in it and silence in it and enough honesty to be useful. And a refusal to let the urgent eat the essential, held in place not by willpower but by a settled conviction that the hour on the knees is the most productive hour of the day.

They did not find time to pray. No one ever finds it. They took it, from things that screamed louder and mattered less.

sections.title: Begin Again Tomorrow Morning
sections.body:
If you have lost it, you have not lost Him. The throne is not crowded. There is no line.

Do not begin by repenting of the last three years, though you may. Begin by showing up tomorrow morning, late and ashamed and out of practice, and saying the truest thing you have said in months, which is that you cannot do this and you forgot it and you need Him. He is not waiting to scold the prodigal. He is watching the road.

Start small and start real. Ten honest minutes beat an hour of performed devotion, and the goal is not to impress God with your discipline but to be with Him until you are changed by it. The prayer life does not return by resolution. It returns by repetition, one kept morning at a time, until the morning you cannot imagine leading without it.

The leader who prays leads from a place no crisis can reach. The leader who does not is one bad week from collapse and does not know it. Choose tomorrow morning. It is the only morning you get to choose.
